requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as a systemd-managed service named inventory-worker on node1
requirements.summary: Unit file /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service created with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, enabled via systemctl enable, and verified active (systemctl is-active/is-enabled returned active/enabled, MainPID=2173 running the correct binary).

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: inventorysvc created as a system account (useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /sbin/nologin), unit file sets User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc, and ps output confirms the running process is owned by inventorysvc (uid 997).

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the public task: os-comparison-worker runs as the systemd-managed 'inventory-worker' service under the dedicated 'inventorysvc' system account on node1, with active/enabled status and correct process ownership directly verified. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed and evidenced end-to-end: healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id fe422859..., service active MainPID=2173), reboot acknowledgement, observed disconnection, reconnection with a differing boot_id (be48fda2...) matching the fixed after_executor snapshot, and confirmed post-restart recovery of the service (active/enabled, new MainPID=872, owned by inventorysvc). No unwanted mutations, residue, or failed services were introduced beyond a trivial reboot log file.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in all three lifecycle snapshots, so native package-manager consistency could not be cross-checked, though this is unrelated to the task's material outcomes.

Evidence for the restart protocol relies on a single reconnect poll cycle rather than multiple health checks over time post-reboot; the recovery window itself appears short but is corroborated by the fixed after_executor snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map directly to the task: discovery (read-only), user/service creation (cmd-ec1e0d8434664db2), and the reboot for the mandatory restart protocol (cmd-fceefbbee5a04351).
